author: Hilary of Poitiers
translation: E. W. Watson & L. Pullan (NPNF 2nd series, vol. 9), public domain
note: Hilary of Poitiers — the 'Athanasius of the West,' the foremost Latin defender of Nicene orthodoxy — grounds the Trinity in the baptismal command (Matthew 28:19): the Father from whom, the Son through whom, the Spirit who pervades all, each One. New author for the corpus. Verified verbatim against source_url (apologia-citations, web, 2026-08-24; translator Watson & Pullan, NPNF2 vol. 9, confirmed).
text: For God the Father is One, from Whom are all things; and our Lord Jesus Christ the Only-begotten, through Whom are all things, is One; and the Spirit, God's Gift to us, Who pervades all things, is also One.
